study type: Case study and inception cohort comparison
cohort: The cohort consisted of 18 pregnant women (6 with Spinal Cord Injury and 12 without Spinal Cord Injury) who completed data collection and were matched by age, parity, and race.
finding: Women with Spinal Cord Injury (SCI) tend to experience more complicated pregnancies, labor, and deliveries, including higher rates of UTIs, and deliver newborns with significantly smaller head circumferences and generally lower birth weight and length compared to non-SCI peers.
birth_weight: Average 2854 g for women with SCI and 3578 g for women without SCI
